frames.title: SubInvoker.Apply
frames.explanation: Every step here names a token that appears MORE THAN ONCE in its own range, so the only thing that decides which glyph is marked is `occurrence`. The renderer counts qualifying matches across the whole range, not per line — steps 5 and 6 are what prove that.

relations.note: the value read on 77, into the guard on 81 — the FROM end is the second `running` on its line

steps.note: The assignment TARGET — leftmost `running` on line 77.
steps.ttsText: The running total is reassigned here, and the name appears twice on this one line. Occurrence one is the target being written.

steps.note: The ARGUMENT — same line, same token, one occurrence later. If this marks the same glyph as the step before, occurrence is being ignored.
steps.ttsText: Occurrence two is the same name used as the argument, further right on the same line.

steps.explanation: A dotted token, twice on a line
steps.note: `guarded.Amount` is not a bare identifier — the whole-word test has to accept a dot on neither flank.
steps.ttsText: The rounded amount is compared against the original, so the same dotted expression appears twice on this line.
Occurrence two is the right-hand side of that comparison.

steps.explanation: Counting ACROSS lines, not within one
steps.note: Occurrence 1 is the declaration on line 68; occurrence 2 is the call on line 77. The count runs over the whole range.
steps.ttsText: The method's own name appears twice in this range — once where it is declared and once where an adjustment's own Apply is called.

steps.note: Four in this range: one on 76, two on 77, one on 78. This is the boundary case that must still resolve.
steps.ttsText: Across these three lines the running total is named four times, and this is the fourth.

steps.explanation: One past the end — validate and drop
steps.note: There is no fifth. The step must still render its lines and its callout; only the flash is dropped. A step that vanishes here is the defect.
steps.ttsText: Asking for a fifth occurrence when there are four is the validate-and-drop path: the step is unaffected, the pulse simply does not happen.
